title: Hive-bee comb building evolved by gradual modification of simpler bee instincts

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Hive-bee comb building evolved by gradual modification of simpler bee instincts

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The cell-making instinct of the hive-bee was acquired through natural selection by slight successive modifications of simpler instincts, of the kind seen in a graded series from humble-bees through Melipona to the hive-bee.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: By such modifications of instincts in themselves not very wonderful,—hardly more wonderful than those which guide a bird to make its nest,—I believe that the hive-bee has acquired, through natural selection, her inimitable architectural powers.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Hive-bee, its cell-making instinct”. Scope: social bees (bumble-bees, stingless bees, honey-bees)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A focused synthesis can test whether comparative states fit gradual evolution. Existing open data are incomplete and discriminate imperfectly among alternative historical sequences.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify comb-building behaviours and architectures across bumblebees, stingless bees, and honeybees, then reconstruct ancestral transitions on a bee phylogeny. Ordered small changes toward regular comb support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nest architecture and construction behaviour are not broadly standardized in open databases.

Modern grades do not uniquely establish the historical route.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.5

discriminating power: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data existence: 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Relationships among the social bees Darwin arranged in a series are recoverable from public sequences and trees, so his particular order can be checked. The architectural measurements that would show slight successive modification are not in those databases. The test can support or upset the proposed sequence for this narrow clade and still leave the selective cause unmeasured.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Order comb architecture, from irregular brood cells through intermediate stingless-bee combs to the hive-bee cell, on a corbiculate-bee phylogeny. A stepwise increase along the tree supports acquisition by successive modification; a phylogeny in which the architectural series is not a historical sequence, or a jump to hexagonal comb without intermediates, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Quantitative nest-architecture scores are in papers, not in the sequence or tree databases.

A grade series of living bees can be ecological rather than the ancestral path.

Many stingless-bee nests are described qualitatively.
